doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Growing up in Oriskany and early teachers
summary: A village with little music, but teacher Frank Galime, Jack Adams, chorus and All-State groups broadened him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: We’ll talk more about that. I’m wondering if you felt like a big fish in a small pond growing up in Oriskany? For those people who are watching this, Oriskany is like a little adjoining town to Utica.

Yeah. It’s not even a town it’s a village. But yeah, I mean in the town itself there really wasn’t that much going on. I mean we had the chorus and the band, and I had a great teacher, Frank Galime, he was the person who really kept me going for a long time, and then he introduced me to you, and also Jack Adams from Holland Patent. So simultaneously I had outside instruction, and that allowed me to go on to around to New York State NYSSMA competitions and I got involved, in chorus, I was singing in All- State Chorus and playing in All-State bands. So I had an opportunity to grow a little bit outside of the surroundings of Oriskany.
Was your whole childhood in Oriskany?
Yeah. From birth. I was born in Utica, but, you know, I lived in Oriskany. So I graduated high school from there.
